sheets.title: Q2 · Principle of superposition of waves (3 marks)
sheets.source: PYQ Nov 2021 (CBCSS) Q2 · also Nov 2019 Q15, Nov 2018 Q21

cards.label: PYQ · 3 marks
cards.title: Question 2
cards.q: Discuss the principle of superposition of waves.
Vector/algebraic sum of individual displacements and mathematical expression

options.t: Principle stated clearly with \(y = y1 + y2\) + ... and linearity/independence noted

cards.why: State that the resultant displacement at any point and instant is the vector sum of the individual displacements.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Principle of superposition of waves
cards.body: Know first: Superposition of two sinusoidal waves. When two or more wave trains travel simultaneously through the same region of a linear medium, each wave propagates independently, and the resultant displacement \( \mathbf{y} \) at any point and instant is the vector (or algebraic) sum of the displacements produced by the individual waves acting alone: \( \mathbf{y} = \mathbf{y}_1 + \mathbf{y}_2 + \dots \). This principle forms the basis of interference and diffraction.

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Linear superposition of wave disturbances
cards.tex: y(x,t) = y_1(x,t) + y_2(x,t) + \dots + y_n(x,t) \\ \text{For two waves in one plane: } y = a_1\sin(\omega t + \phi_1) + a_2\sin(\omega t + \phi_2)
cards.body: State the vector/algebraic sum rule and note that it holds because the wave differential equation is linear. Statement 2 · equation & significance 1.

cards.q: The principle of superposition holds in media where the wave equation is ____.
cards.why: Any linear combination of solutions of a linear differential equation is also a solution.

cards.q: According to the superposition principle, when two waves cross each other, they afterward ____.
cards.why: Each wave retains its own amplitude, frequency, and direction after passing through the overlap region.

cards.q: When two crests of equal amplitude \( a \) meet in phase, the resultant displacement is ____.
cards.why: Algebraic addition gives \(y = a + a = 2a\).

sheets.title: Q3 · Coherence time and coherence length (3 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 3 marks
cards.title: Question 3
cards.q: Explain the terms coherence time and coherence length.
Definitions and relations \(\tau_c\) ~ \(1/\Delta \nu\) and \(l_c = c \cdot \tau_c = \lambda^2 / \Delta \lambda\)

options.t: Both coherence time and coherence length defined with formulas
Definitions without formulas or only one defined

cards.why: Define both temporal coherence parameters and write their mathematical relations.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Coherence time and coherence length
cards.body: Know first: Interference of light waves. Coherence time \( \tau_c \) is the average time interval over which a light wave train maintains a predictable sinusoidal phase without random phase jumps; it is inversely proportional to the spectral bandwidth, \( \tau_c \approx 1/\Delta\nu \). Coherence length \( l_c \) is the spatial length of this coherent wave train, given by \( l_c = c\tau_c = \frac{c}{\Delta\nu} = \frac{\lambda^2}{\Delta\lambda} \).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Relations for temporal coherence
cards.body: Define coherence time \(\tau_c\) and coherence length \(l_c = c \cdot \tau_c\) and relate them to spectral line width \(\Delta \lambda\). Coherence time 1.5 · coherence length 1.5.

cards.q: Coherence length \( l_c \) is related to coherence time \( \tau_c \) by ____.
cards.why: Distance travelled by light in time \(\tau_c\) is \(c \cdot \tau_c\).

cards.q: In terms of wavelength \( \lambda \) and spectral width \( \Delta\lambda \), coherence length equals ____.
cards.why: Since \(|\Delta \nu| = c \Delta \lambda / \lambda^2\), \(l_c = c / \Delta \nu = \lambda^2 / \Delta \lambda\).

cards.q: A highly monochromatic laser source with a very narrow spectral width \( \Delta\nu \) has a ____.
cards.why: Smaller \(\Delta \nu\) yields larger \(\tau_c\) and longer coherence length \(l_c\).

sheets.title: Q4 · Rayleigh criterion of resolution (3 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 3 marks
cards.title: Question 4
cards.q: Discuss the Rayleigh criterion of resolution.
Statement of central maximum falling on first minimum and dip in resultant intensity

options.t: Principal maximum of one coincides with first minimum of the other, with angular limit or intensity dip stated

cards.why: State Rayleigh's condition for two just-resolved diffraction patterns and give the angular separation.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Rayleigh's criterion for just-resolved images
cards.body: Know first: N-slit Fraunhofer diffraction pattern and grating. According to Lord Rayleigh's criterion, two equally bright point sources or spectral lines are just resolved when the central principal maximum of the diffraction pattern of one falls exactly on the first minimum of the diffraction pattern of the other. At this separation (\( \theta_{\min} = \frac{1.22\lambda}{D} \) for a circular aperture), the resultant intensity curve shows a distinct central dip of about \( 8/\pi^2 \approx 81\% \) of either peak.

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Rayleigh condition for slits and circular apertures
cards.body: State the coincidence of the principal maximum of one pattern with the first minimum of the second and note the resulting saddle dip. Criterion 2 · formula/dip 1.

cards.q: At Rayleigh's limit of resolution for two slit patterns, the intensity at the midpoint dip is approximately ____.
If the angular separation of two point sources is less than \( 1.22\lambda/D \), the images are ____.
cards.why: Separations smaller than the Rayleigh limit merge into a single unresolved peak.

cards.q: Using shorter-wavelength light in a microscope or telescope makes the limit of resolution \( \theta_{\min} \) ____.
cards.why: \(\theta_{min} = 1.22 \lambda / D\) is directly proportional to wavelength \(\lambda\).

sheets.title: Q5 · Maxima and minima conditions for Newton's rings (3 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 3 marks
cards.title: Question 5
cards.q: Write down the conditions for maxima and minima for the Newton's rings in the reflected system.
Effective path difference and conditions for bright and dark rings in reflected light

options.t: Path difference 2nt + \(\lambda/2\) and both maxima and minima conditions stated
Only one condition stated or phase shift omitted

cards.why: Include the \(\lambda/2\) phase shift at the lower glass plate and write the conditions for bright and dark rings.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Reflected Newton's rings maxima and minima
cards.body: Know first: Colours of thin films, Newton's rings, Michelson interferometer (11). For near-normal incidence on a film of refractive index \( n \) and thickness \( t = r^2/(2R) \), reflection at the lower optically denser plate introduces an extra path difference of \( \lambda/2 \), so \( \Delta = 2nt + \lambda/2 \). Thus, maxima (bright rings) occur when \( 2nt = (2m - 1)\frac{\lambda}{2} \), and minima (dark rings) occur when \( 2nt = m\lambda \) (with \( m = 0, 1, 2, \dots \), making the central spot dark).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Film thickness and ring radius conditions
cards.tex: \Delta = 2nt + \frac{\lambda}{2}, \quad t = \frac{r^2}{2R} \\ \text{Maxima (bright): } 2nt = (2m - 1)\frac{\lambda}{2} \implies r_m = \sqrt{\frac{(2m - 1)\lambda R}{2n}} \\ \text{Minima (dark): } 2nt = m\lambda \implies r_m = \sqrt{\frac{m\lambda R}{n}}
cards.body: State the total path difference including the \(\lambda/2\) reflection shift and write the thickness/radius equations for maxima and minima. Path difference 1 · maxima 1 · minima 1.

cards.q: In the reflected Newton's rings system with an air film, the central spot (\( t = 0 \)) is ____.
cards.why: At \(t = 0\), the path difference is \(\lambda/2\) due to reflection at the lower glass surface.

cards.q: In reflected light, the condition for the \( m \)-th dark Newton's ring in an air film (\( n = 1 \)) is \( 2t \) equal to ____.
cards.why: \(2t + \lambda/2 = (2m+1)\lambda/2\) simplifies to \(2t = m \lambda\).

cards.q: The diameter of the \( m \)-th dark Newton's ring is proportional to the ____.
cards.why: \(D_m = 2 \sqrt{m \lambda R / n}\) is proportional to \(\sqrt{m}\).

sheets.title: Q7 · Huygens wave surfaces in a positive doubly refracting crystal (3 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 3 marks
cards.title: Question 7
cards.q: Show a figure illustrating the Huygens wave surfaces produced by a point source embedded in a positive doubly refracting crystal.
Diagram showing outer sphere (o-ray) and inner ellipsoid (e-ray) touching along the optic axis

options.t: Neat figure showing ellipsoid inside sphere touching along the optic axis with labels
Figure without labels or reversed surfaces

cards.why: For a positive crystal (ne > no, ve < vo), the e-wave ellipsoid lies inside the o-wave sphere.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Huygens wave surfaces in a positive uniaxial crystal
cards.body: Know first: Double refraction and Huygens' explanation. In a positive uniaxial crystal (such as quartz, \( n_e > n_o \)), the velocity of the extraordinary ray perpendicular to the optic axis is less than that of the ordinary ray (\( v_{re} = c/n_e < v_{ro} = c/n_o \)). Therefore, the prolate ellipsoid of revolution (e-ray wavefront) lies completely inside the sphere (o-ray wavefront), touching it along the optic axis where \( v_{re} = v_{ro} = c/n_o \).
cards.tex: n_e > n_o \implies v_e < v_o \text{ (ellipsoid inside sphere)}

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Radii of o-wave sphere and e-wave ellipsoid
cards.body: Draw an outer circle of radius c/no and an inner ellipse of semi-minor axis c/ne touching along the optic axis. Diagram 2 · labels & explanation 1.

cards.q: In a positive uniaxial crystal like quartz, the ellipsoid of revolution lies ____.
cards.why: Since \(n_e > n_o\), \(v_e = c/n_e < c/n_o = v_o\) perpendicular to the optic axis.

cards.q: For a positive doubly refracting crystal, the birefringence \( n_e - n_o \) is ____.
cards.why: Positive crystals are defined by \(n_e > n_o\).

cards.q: An example of a positive uniaxial crystal is ____.
cards.why: Quartz has \(n_o = 1.544\) and \(n_e = 1.553\).

sheets.title: Q8 · Production of elliptically polarized light (3 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 3 marks
cards.title: Question 8
cards.q: How is an elliptically polarized light produced ?
Passing linearly polarized light through a quarter-wave plate at angle \(\theta\) != 0, 45, 90 degrees

options.t: Linearly polarized light incident on a QWP at an angle other than 0, 45 or 90 degrees to the optic axis explained
Mentions QWP without specifying the unequal-amplitude angle condition

cards.why: Explain how two orthogonal components of unequal amplitude with \(a \pi/2\) phase difference form elliptically polarized light.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Production of elliptically polarized light
cards.body: Know first: Production and analysis of polarised light (22). Elliptically polarized light is produced by passing a linearly polarized light beam normally through a quarter-wave plate (QWP) such that the electric vector of the incident beam makes an angle \( \phi \) (other than \( 0^\circ, 45^\circ, 90^\circ \)) with the optic axis. Inside the QWP, the beam splits into ordinary and extraordinary components of unequal amplitudes \( E_0\sin\phi \) and \( E_0\cos\phi \) with a phase difference of \( \pi/2 \), which recombine on emergence to trace an ellipse.

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Ellipse equation from a quarter-wave plate
cards.tex: E_x = E_0\sin\phi\sin\omega t, \quad E_y = E_0\cos\phi\cos\omega t \\ \frac{E_x^2}{(E_0\sin\phi)^2} + \frac{E_y^2}{(E_0\cos\phi)^2} = \sin^2\omega t + \cos^2\omega t = 1
cards.body: Resolve the incident amplitude E0 along and perpendicular to the optic axis of a QWP with \(\phi\) != 45 degrees and combine with \(a \pi/2\) phase shift. Setup/angle condition 1.5 · wave equation 1.5.

cards.q: To produce elliptically polarized light using a quarter-wave plate, the incident linear polarization must make an angle with the optic axis ____.
cards.why: At 45 degrees the amplitudes are equal (giving circular polarization); at 0 or 90 degrees only one wave exists (linear).

cards.q: A quarter-wave plate introduces a phase difference between the o-ray and e-ray equal to ____.
cards.why: A path difference of \(\lambda/4\) corresponds to a phase difference of \(\pi/2\).

cards.q: In elliptically polarized light, the magnitude of the electric field vector ____.
options: oscillates along a fixed straight line
cards.why: The tip of the electric vector traces an ellipse, varying between the semi-major and semi-minor axes.

sheets.title: Q9 · Dextrorotatory vs laevorotatory substances (3 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 3 marks
cards.title: Question 9
cards.q: Distinguish between dextrorotatory and laevorotatory substances.
Rotation direction, refractive index inequality (nL vs nR), and examples

options.t: Clockwise vs anticlockwise rotation (facing the source), nL > nR vs nL < nR, and examples given

cards.why: Compare rotation sense, circular refractive indices, and examples.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Dextrorotatory and laevorotatory substances
cards.body: Know first: Production and analysis of polarised light (22). Dextrorotatory (right-handed) substances rotate the plane of polarization clockwise when looking towards the oncoming light beam; for them \( n_L > n_R \) (RCP travels faster than LCP, e.g., cane sugar solution, d-quartz). Laevorotatory (left-handed) substances rotate the plane of polarization anticlockwise; for them \( n_L < n_R \) (LCP travels faster than RCP, e.g., fruit sugar/fructose, l-quartz).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Fresnel rotation sign condition
cards.tex: \phi(z) = \frac{\pi}{\lambda}(n_L - n_R)z \\ n_L > n_R \implies v_R > v_L \implies \phi > 0 \text{ (dextrorotatory)} \\ n_L < n_R \implies v_L > v_R \implies \phi < 0 \text{ (laevorotatory)}
cards.body: Contrast the direction of rotation, circular wave velocities, and examples for both classes. Direction of rotation 1.5 · nL vs nR & examples 1.5.

cards.q: A substance that rotates the plane of polarization clockwise (looking against the beam) is ____.
cards.why: Dextro means right-handed (clockwise).

cards.q: In a dextrorotatory medium, the circularly polarized component that travels faster is the ____.
cards.why: Since nL > nR, vR = c/nR > c/nL = vL.

cards.q: Quartz crystals exist in both dextrorotatory and laevorotatory forms because of their ____.
cards.why: Enantiomorphic quartz crystals have opposite spiral arrangements of SiO2 tetrahedra.

sheets.title: Q10 · Basic steps in holography (3 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 3 marks
cards.title: Question 10
cards.q: Discuss the basic steps in holography.
Two-step process: recording (interference) and reconstruction (diffraction)

options.t: Both recording of interference pattern and reconstruction by diffraction explained

cards.why: Explain both the recording step and the reconstruction step.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Recording and reconstruction in holography
cards.body: Know first: Interference of light waves. Holography consists of two basic steps: (1) Recording (construction), where a coherent laser beam is split into a reference wave \( E_R \) and an object-scattered wave \( E_O \) that interfere on a high-resolution photographic plate to record both amplitude and phase as fringes; and (2) Reconstruction, where the developed hologram is illuminated by the reference beam \( E_R \) alone, diffracting light to recreate the original 3D virtual image and a conjugate real image.
cards.tex: \text{Step 1: } I = |E_R + E_O|^2; \quad \text{Step 2: } T E_R \to E_O + E_O^*

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Interference recording and diffraction readout
cards.tex: \text{1. Recording (Interference): } I = |E_R + E_O|^2 = I_R + I_O + E_R^* E_O + E_R E_O^* \\ \text{2. Reconstruction (Diffraction): } E_{\text{out}} \propto I \cdot E_R = (I_R + I_O)E_R + I_R E_O + E_R^2 E_O^*
cards.body: Describe the two steps: interference during recording and diffraction during reconstruction. Recording step 1.5 · reconstruction step 1.5.

cards.q: The first basic step of holography (recording the hologram) is based on the principle of ____.
cards.why: The object wave and reference wave interfere on the photographic plate.

cards.q: The second basic step of holography (reading out the image) is based on the principle of ____.
cards.why: The reference wave is diffracted by the recorded fringe pattern.

cards.q: During reconstruction, the observer looking through the hologram sees a three-dimensional ____.
cards.why: The diffracted wave \(I_R E_O\) diverges from the original object location.

sheets.title: Q11 · Step-index vs graded-index optical fibers (3 marks)
sheets.source: PYQ Nov 2021 (CBCSS) Q11 · also Nov 2020 Q24

cards.label: PYQ · 3 marks
cards.title: Question 11
cards.q: Distinguish between step index and graded index optical fibers.
Comparison of refractive index profile, ray trajectories, and pulse dispersion

options.t: Index profile (uniform vs parabolic), ray path (zig-zag vs sinusoidal), and dispersion/bandwidth compared

cards.why: Contrast core refractive index profile, ray path geometry, and intermodal dispersion.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Comparison of step-index and graded-index fibers
cards.body: Know first: Laws of reflection and refraction from Fermat's principle. (1) In a step-index fiber, the core refractive index \( n_1 \) is uniform throughout and drops abruptly to \( n_2 \) at the cladding boundary; in a graded-index (GRIN) fiber, the core index decreases continuously (parabolically) from the axis to \( n_2 \). (2) Rays travel in straight zig-zag paths by sharp total internal reflection in step-index fibers, but follow smooth sinusoidal curved paths by continuous refraction in GRIN fibers. (3) GRIN fibers have much lower intermodal pulse dispersion and higher bandwidth.

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Dispersion comparison
cards.body: Compare refractive index distribution, ray trajectories, and modal dispersion. Index profile 1 · ray paths 1 · dispersion/bandwidth 1.

cards.q: In a step-index optical fiber, the meridional rays propagate along ____.
cards.why: Constant core index n1 gives straight ray segments between reflections at the core wall.

cards.q: In a graded-index fiber, rays travelling farther from the axis move faster because the refractive index there is ____.
cards.why: Local phase velocity \(v = c/n(r)\) increases as n(r) decreases radially.

cards.q: The intermodal pulse broadening in a parabolic graded-index fiber is proportional to ____.
cards.why: Parabolic grading cancels first-order delay, leaving a small \(\Delta^2\) term.

sheets.title: Q12 · Basic parts of a fiber optic sensor (3 marks)
sheets.source: PYQ Nov 2021 (CBCSS) Q12 · also Nov 2020 Q22

cards.label: PYQ · 3 marks
cards.title: Question 12
cards.q: Discuss the basic parts of a fiber optic sensor.
Optical source, optical fiber & sensing/transducer element, and photodetector/processing unit

options.t: Source, fiber/sensing zone (modulator), and detector/signal processor explained

cards.why: Identify and explain the source, fiber transducer/modulation zone, and detector.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Basic components of a fiber optic sensor
cards.body: Know first: Laws of reflection and refraction from Fermat's principle. A fiber optic sensor system consists of: (1) an optical source (LED or laser diode) that launches light into the fiber, (2) the optical fiber and sensing/transducer region where the measurand (temperature, pressure, strain, or magnetic field) modulates the intensity, phase, polarization, or wavelength of the guided light, and (3) a photodetector and electronic signal processor that converts the modulated optical signal into a measurable electrical output.

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Signal modulation in fiber sensor
cards.body: Describe the optical source, the intrinsic/extrinsic fiber sensing element, and the optical detector/demodulator. Source 1 · sensing fiber 1 · detector 1.

cards.q: In an intrinsic fiber optic sensor, the modulation of the light beam takes place ____.
cards.why: In an intrinsic sensor, the fiber itself acts as the sensing element.

cards.q: The component at the receiving end of a fiber optic sensor that converts light into electrical current is a ____.
cards.why: A photodiode or photodetector converts optical power into photocurrent.

cards.q: Fiber optic sensors are ideal for hazardous environments because they are immune to ____.
cards.why: Dielectric glass fibers do not conduct electricity or pick up RF interference.

sheets.title: Q13 · Derivation of Newtonian lens formula (5 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 5 marks
cards.title: Question 13
cards.q: Obtain the Newtonian lens formula.
Ray diagram and similar-triangle derivation of \(f1 f2 = x1\times2\) (or \(x1\times2 = -f^2\))

options.t: Clear ray diagram, similar triangle ratios -y'/\(y = -f1/(-x1) = x2/f2\), and \(f1 f2 = x1\times2 (x1\times2 = -f^2)\) derived
Derivation without diagram or missing sign explanation

cards.why: Use similar triangles at the first and second principal foci to derive \(f1 f2 = x1\times2\).

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Newtonian lens formula \(f1 f2 = x1\times2\)
cards.body: Know first: The Newton formula and lateral magnification. Let \( x_1 \) be the axial distance of the object from the first principal focus \( F_1 \) and \( x_2 \) be the axial distance of the image from the second principal focus \( F_2 \). From similar triangles at \( F_1 \) and \( F_2 \), \( \frac{-y'}{y} = \frac{-f_1}{-x_1} \) and \( \frac{-y'}{y} = \frac{x_2}{f_2} \), which gives \( f_1 f_2 = x_1 x_2 \). When the medium on both sides is the same (\( f_2 = -f_1 = f \)), this becomes \( x_1 x_2 = -f^2 \).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Derivation from similar triangles at F1 and F2
cards.tex: \text{From similar triangles } AOF_1 \text{ and } LPF_1: \quad \frac{-y'}{y} = \frac{-f_1}{-x_1} = \frac{f_1}{x_1} \\ \text{From similar triangles } KPF_2 \text{ and } BIF_2: \quad \frac{-y'}{y} = \frac{x_2}{f_2} \\ \frac{f_1}{x_1} = \frac{x_2}{f_2} \implies f_1 f_2 = x_1 x_2 \\ \text{For identical media on both sides } (f_2 = -f_1 = f): \quad x_1 x_2 = -f^2
cards.body: Equate the height ratios -y'/y from the two pairs of similar focal triangles. Diagram 1.5 · triangle ratios 2 · final Newton formula 1.5.

cards.label: Derivation
cards.title: Newton's lens formula, step by step
cards.legend: Object \(OA\) at distance \(x_1\) from \(F_1\), image \(IB\) at distance \(x_2\) from \(F_2\), for a thin lens with focal length \(f\) on both sides.

phases.name: First focal triangles
phases.why: similar triangles on the object side

phases.name: Second focal triangles
phases.why: similar triangles on the image side

phases.name: Equating ratios
phases.why: both expressions give the same magnification

phases.name: Identical surrounding media
phases.why: f1 and f2 have equal magnitude

steps.note: Similar triangles \(AOF_1\) and \(LPF_1\) give the magnification in terms of \(x_1\).
Similar triangles \(KPF_2\) and \(BIF_2\) give the same ratio in terms of \(x_2\).

ask.q: From which reference points are \(x_1\) and \(x_2\) measured?
ask.why: Newton's formula uses distances from the two focal points, not from the lens.

steps.note: Equate the two expressions for \(y'/y\).

ask.q: What relation follows by equating the two expressions for \(y'/y\)?
ask.why: Cancelling the common minus sign leaves one ratio on each side.

steps.note: Multiply both sides by \(x_1 f\) to clear the fractions.

ask.q: Why do the two focal lengths in this formula have equal magnitude?
ask.why: With the same medium on both sides, \(f_1 = -f_2\) in magnitude.

steps.note: With Cartesian signs, \(x_1\) and \(x_2\) take opposite signs, so the product is negative.

ask.q: For the same medium on both sides, what are the focal lengths?
ask.why: Equal media give focal lengths of equal magnitude and opposite sign.

cards.q: In Newton's lens formula \( x_1 x_2 = -f^2 \), \( x_1 \) and \( x_2 \) must always have ____.
cards.why: Because -\(f^2 < 0\), one distance is positive and the other is negative.

cards.q: In terms of extrafocal distance \( x_1 \) and first focal length \( f_1 \), lateral magnification \( m \) is ____.
If an object is placed at a distance \( 2f \) to the left of \( F_1 \) (\( x_1 = -2f \)), then \( x_2 \) is ____.

sheets.title: Q14 · Separation between coherent sources in a biprism (5 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 5 marks
cards.title: Question 14
cards.q: Determine the separation between the coherent sources formed by a biprism whose inclined faces make angles of \(2^{\circ}\) with its base and the slit is 0.1 m away from the biprism. Given, the refractive index of the material of the prism is 1.5.
Conversion of 2 degrees to radians and calculation of \(d = 2a(n-1)\alpha\)

options.t: Formula \(d = 2a(n-1)\alpha\), radian conversion, and \(d = 3.49\times 10^{-3}\) m (3.49 mm)
Formula and substitution without converting degrees to radians

cards.why: Convert \(\alpha = 2\) degrees to radians and evaluate \(d = 2a(n-1)\alpha\).

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Source separation \(d = 3.49\) mm
cards.body: Know first: Fresnel's two-mirror and Fresnel's biprism. The separation between the two virtual coherent sources formed by a biprism is \( d = 2a(n - 1)\alpha \). With \( a = 0.1\text{ m} \), \( n = 1.5 \), and \( \alpha = 2^\circ = 2 \times \frac{\pi}{180}\text{ rad} = 0.03491\text{ rad} \), we obtain \( d = 2(0.1)(0.5)(0.03491) = 3.491\times 10^{-3}\text{ m} = 3.49\text{ mm} \).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Calculation of virtual source separation
cards.tex: \alpha = 2^\circ = 2 \times \frac{\pi}{180}\text{ rad} = 0.03491\text{ rad} \\ a = 0.1\text{ m}, \quad n = 1.5 \\ d = 2a(n - 1)\alpha = 2 \times 0.1 \times (1.5 - 1) \times 0.03491 \\ d = 0.1 \times 0.03491 = 3.491 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m} = 3.49\text{ mm}
cards.body: Convert the refracting angle 2 degrees to radians and substitute into \(d = 2a(n - 1)\alpha\). Formula 1.5 · radian conversion 1.5 · result 2.

cards.q: Fresnel's biprism produces two coherent virtual sources by ____.
options: refraction through two thin acute prisms
cards.why: The two halves of the biprism refract light from a single slit to form two virtual images.

cards.q: If the distance \( a \) between the slit and the biprism is doubled, the separation \( d \) between the virtual sources ____.
cards.why: \(d = 2a(n - 1)\alpha\) is directly proportional to a.

cards.q: For a biprism whose base angles are \( \alpha = 2^\circ \), the obtuse vertex angle of the prism is ____.
cards.why: \(180 - 2\)*(2 degrees) = 176 degrees.

sheets.title: Q15 · Radius of first dark ring in circular aperture diffraction (5 marks)
sheets.source: PYQ Nov 2021 (CBCSS) Q15 · also Nov 2022 (CBCSS) Q15

cards.label: PYQ · 5 marks
cards.title: Question 15
cards.q: Calculate the radius of the first dark ring of the Fraunhofer diffraction pattern produced by a circular aperture of radius 0.02 cm at the focal plane of a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. Assume that the wavelength of light used is 600 nm.
Formula \(R1 = 1.22 f \lambda / D\) (with \(D = 2a = 0.04\) cm) and numerical result

options.t: Used radius 0.02 cm as diameter D, giving 0.732 mm

cards.why: Note that aperture radius is \(a = 0.02\) cm, so diameter \(D = 2a = 0.04\) cm.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: First dark ring radius \(R1 = 0.366\) mm
cards.body: Know first: Single-slit Fraunhofer diffraction pattern (12). For a circular aperture of radius \( a = 0.02\text{ cm} \) (diameter \( D = 2a = 0.04\text{ cm} = 4\times 10^{-4}\text{ m} \)), the radius of the first dark ring at the focal plane (\( f = 0.20\text{ m} \)) for \( \lambda = 600\text{ nm} \) is \( R_1 = \frac{1.22 f\lambda}{D} = 3.66\times 10^{-4}\text{ m} = 0.366\text{ mm} \) (and the second dark ring in Nov 2022 Q15 is \( R_2 = \frac{2.233 f\lambda}{D} = 0.670\text{ mm} \)).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Airy dark ring radius calculation
cards.tex: a = 0.02\text{ cm} \implies D = 2a = 0.04\text{ cm} = 4 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m} \\ f = 20\text{ cm} = 0.20\text{ m}, \quad \lambda = 600\text{ nm} = 6 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m} \\ R_1 = f\theta_1 = \frac{1.22 f\lambda}{D} = \frac{1.22 \times 0.20 \times 6 \times 10^{-7}}{4 \times 10^{-4}} = 3.66 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m} = 0.366\text{ mm} \\ R_2 = \frac{2.233 f\lambda}{D} = \frac{2.233 \times 0.20 \times 6 \times 10^{-7}}{4 \times 10^{-4}} = 6.70 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m} = 0.670\text{ mm}
cards.body: Double the given aperture radius to get diameter \(D = 2a = 0.04\) cm, then apply \(R1 = 1.22 f \lambda / D\). Formula 1.5 · \(D = 2a\) substitution 1.5 · final answer 2.

cards.q: In terms of the aperture radius \( a \), the angular radius of the first dark Airy ring is ____.
cards.why: \(1.22 \lambda / D = 1.22 \lambda / (2a) = 0.61 \lambda / a\).

cards.q: The linear radius \( R_1 \) of the first dark ring in the focal plane of a lens of focal length \( f \) is ____.
cards.why: For small diffraction angles, \(R1 = f \tan(\theta1)\) ~ \(f \cdot \theta1\).

cards.q: If the focal length \( f \) of the focusing lens is doubled, the radius of the Airy disc on the screen ____.
cards.why: \(R1 = 1.22 f \lambda / D\) is directly proportional to f.

sheets.title: Q16 · Positions of foci of a Fresnel zone plate (5 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 5 marks
cards.title: Question 16
cards.q: Consider a Fresnel zone plate with radii \(r_n = 0.1\sqrt{n}\) cm. For \(\lambda = 5 \times 10^{-5}\) cm, calculate the positions of the foci.
Principal focal length \(f1 = r1^2 / \lambda\) and higher-order foci fm = \(f1 / (2m-1)\)

options.t: \(f1 = 200\) cm (2 m) and higher-order foci \(f2 = 66.7\) cm, \(f3 = 40\) cm, ... calculated

cards.why: Identify \(r1 = 0.1\) cm, calculate principal focus \(f1 = r1^2 / \lambda = 200\) cm, and list odd-fraction secondary foci.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Foci at 200 cm, 66.7 cm, 40 cm, ...
cards.body: Know first: Fresnel diffraction and zone plate (15). Comparing \( r_n = 0.1\sqrt{n}\text{ cm} \) with \( r_n = \sqrt{n f_1 \lambda} \), the first-zone radius is \( r_1 = 0.1\text{ cm} \). With \( \lambda = 5\times 10^{-5}\text{ cm} \), the principal focus is at \( f_1 = \frac{r_1^2}{\lambda} = \frac{0.01}{5\times 10^{-5}} = 200\text{ cm} = 2\text{ m} \), and the higher-order foci are at \( f_m = \frac{f_1}{2m-1} = 200\text{ cm}, 66.7\text{ cm}, 40\text{ cm}, 28.6\text{ cm}, \dots \).
cards.tex: f_1 = 200\text{ cm}, \; f_2 = 66.7\text{ cm}, \; f_3 = 40\text{ cm}, \dots

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Calculation of principal and secondary foci
cards.tex: r_n = 0.1\sqrt{n}\text{ cm} \implies r_1 = 0.1\text{ cm}, \quad \lambda = 5 \times 10^{-5}\text{ cm} \\ f_1 = \frac{r_1^2}{\lambda} = \frac{(0.1)^2}{5 \times 10^{-5}} = \frac{10^{-2}}{5 \times 10^{-5}} = 200\text{ cm} = 2.0\text{ m} \\ f_m = \frac{r_1^2}{(2m - 1)\lambda} = \frac{f_1}{2m - 1}, \quad m = 1, 2, 3, \dots \\ f_1 = 200\text{ cm}, \quad f_2 = \frac{200}{3} = 66.67\text{ cm}, \quad f_3 = \frac{200}{5} = 40\text{ cm}
cards.body: Find r1 from the given expression rn = \(0.1 \sqrt{n}\) cm, compute \(f1 = r1^2 / \lambda\), and divide by odd integers 3, 5, ... for secondary foci. r1 & f1 3 · secondary foci fm 2.

cards.q: The secondary foci of a zone plate of principal focal length \( f_1 \) are located at distances ____.
cards.why: When each open zone encompasses 3, 5, 7, ... half-period zones, a weaker focus is formed.

cards.q: Among all the foci of a zone plate, the most intense focus is at ____.
cards.why: At f1 each transparent ring contains a single uncancelled half-period zone.

cards.q: If \( r_n = 0.1\sqrt{n}\text{ cm} \), the radius of the 4th zone \( r_4 \) is ____.

sheets.title: Q17 · Thickness of quartz half-wave plate (5 marks)
sheets.source: PYQ Nov 2021 (CBCSS) Q17 · also Nov 2020 Q28

cards.label: PYQ · 5 marks
cards.title: Question 17
cards.q: Determine the thickness of a half-wave plate of quartz for a wavelength 500 nm. Given, the refractive indices of the extra-ordinary and ordinary rays are \(\mu_e = 1.553\) and \(\mu_o = 1.544\), respectively.
Formula \(t = \lambda / [2(\mu_e - \mu_o)]\) and numerical result

options.t: Formula \(t = \lambda / [2(\mu_e - \mu_o)]\) and \(t = 2.778\times 10^{-5}\) m (0.0278 mm) (and QWP = 0.0139 mm for Nov 2020)

cards.why: Substitute \(\lambda = 500\times 10^{-9}\) m and \(\mu_e - \mu_o = 0.009\) into \(t = \lambda / [2(\mu_e - \mu_o)]\).

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Half-wave plate thickness \(t = 0.0278\) mm (27.8 um)
cards.body: Know first: Quarter-wave and half-wave plates (21). The minimum thickness of a half-wave plate is \( t_{\text{HWP}} = \frac{\lambda}{2(\mu_e - \mu_o)} \). With \( \lambda = 500\text{ nm} = 5\times 10^{-7}\text{ m} \) and \( \mu_e - \mu_o = 1.553 - 1.544 = 0.009 \), we find \( t_{\text{HWP}} = \frac{5\times 10^{-7}}{2 \times 0.009} = 2.778\times 10^{-5}\text{ m} = 0.0278\text{ mm} \) (and for a quarter-wave plate in Nov 2020 Q28, \( t_{\text{QWP}} = \frac{\lambda}{4(\mu_e - \mu_o)} = 1.389\times 10^{-5}\text{ m} = 0.0139\text{ mm} \)).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Calculation of HWP (and QWP) thickness
cards.tex: \lambda = 500\text{ nm} = 5 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}, \quad \mu_e - \mu_o = 1.553 - 1.544 = 0.009 \\ t_{\text{HWP}} = \frac{\lambda}{2(\mu_e - \mu_o)} = \frac{5 \times 10^{-7}}{2 \times 0.009} = 2.778 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m} = 0.0278\text{ mm} \\ t_{\text{QWP}} = \frac{\lambda}{4(\mu_e - \mu_o)} = \frac{5 \times 10^{-7}}{4 \times 0.009} = 1.389 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m} = 0.0139\text{ mm}
cards.body: Compute the birefringence \(\mu_e - \mu_o = 0.009\) and divide \(\lambda\) by \(2(\mu_e - \mu_o)\). Formula 1.5 · substitution 1.5 · answer with units 2.

cards.q: A half-wave plate introduces an optical path difference between the o-ray and e-ray equal to ____.
cards.why: An odd multiple of \(\lambda/2\) path difference gives a phase difference of \(\pi\).

cards.q: For the same crystal and wavelength, the thickness of a half-wave plate is ____.
options: twice that of a quarter-wave plate
half that of a quarter-wave plate
equal to that of a quarter-wave plate
four times that of a quarter-wave plate
cards.why: \(\lambda / (2 \Delta \mu) = 2 \cdot [\lambda / (4 \Delta \mu)]\).

cards.q: When linearly polarized light at azimuth \( \theta \) to the optic axis passes through a half-wave plate, its plane of polarization rotates by ____.
cards.why: Reversing one component reflects the polarization vector across the optic axis by \(2 \theta\).

sheets.title: Q19 · Numerical aperture and acceptance angle of optical fiber (5 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 5 marks
cards.title: Question 19
cards.q: Calculate the numerical aperture and hence the acceptance angle of an optical fiber having core and cladding refractive indices 1.45 and 1.40 respectively.
Calculation of NA and acceptance angle \(\theta_a\)

options.t: NA = 0.3775 and acceptance angle \(\theta_a = 22.18\) degrees calculated
Only NA = 0.3775 calculated without acceptance angle

cards.why: Compute NA = \(\sqrt{1.45^2 - 1.40^2}\) and take \(\sin^{-1}\)(NA) to get \(\theta_a\).

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: NA = 0.3775 and acceptance angle = 22.18 degrees
cards.body: Know first: Laws of reflection and refraction from Fermat's principle. With \( n_1 = 1.45 \) and \( n_2 = 1.40 \), the numerical aperture is \( \text{NA} = \sqrt{n_1^2 - n_2^2} = \sqrt{1.45^2 - 1.40^2} = \sqrt{0.1425} = 0.3775 \). The acceptance angle in air is \( \theta_a = \sin^{-1}(\text{NA}) = \sin^{-1}(0.3775) = 22.18^\circ \).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Calculation of NA and \(\theta_a\)
cards.body: Evaluate NA from the core and cladding refractive indices, then take the inverse sine for acceptance angle. NA calculation 2.5 · acceptance angle 2.5.

cards.q: In air (\( n_0 = 1 \)), the acceptance angle \( \theta_a \) is related to the numerical aperture by ____.
cards.why: By definition, NA = \(n0 \sin(\theta_a) = \sin(\theta_a)\) in air.

cards.q: If the difference between core and cladding refractive indices increases, the acceptance angle ____.
cards.why: Larger \(n1^2 - n2^2\) gives a larger NA and a wider acceptance cone.

cards.q: The full vertex angle of the acceptance cone of a fiber with acceptance angle \( \theta_a \) is ____.
cards.why: \(\theta_a\) is the half-angle measured from the fiber axis.

sheets.title: Q20 · Interference by a plane parallel film and conditions for maxima and minima (11 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 11 marks
cards.title: Question 20
cards.q: Discuss the interference by a plane parallel film when illuminated by a plane wave and obtain the conditions for maxima and minima.
Ray diagram and geometric derivation of path difference \(2 n d \cos r\)

options.t: Clear ray diagram and derivation of geometric path difference \(\Delta = 2 n d \cos r\) using Snell's law
Diagram with formula stated without full geometric derivation

cards.why: Draw the parallel film ray diagram and prove that n(AB + BC) - AD = \(2 n d \cos r\).

cards.q: Phase shift on reflection and conditions for maxima and minima in reflected and transmitted light

options.t: \(\lambda/2\) reflection shift explained and both maxima and minima conditions obtained
Conditions stated without explaining phase shift

cards.why: Include the Stokes \(\pi\) phase shift at the denser boundary and state constructive and destructive conditions.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Plane parallel thin-film interference
cards.body: Know first: Interference by division of amplitude and non-reflecting films (10). When a plane wave is incident at angle \( i \) on a parallel film of thickness \( d \) and refractive index \( n \) in air, the geometric path difference between rays reflected from the top and bottom surfaces is \( \Delta_{\text{geom}} = n(AB + BC) - AD = 2nd\cos r \), where \( r \) is the angle of refraction. Because reflection at the upper air-to-film surface introduces a phase change of \( \pi \) (extra path \( \lambda/2 \)), the effective path difference in reflected light is \( 2nd\cos r + \lambda/2 \), giving maxima when \( 2nd\cos r = (2m - 1)\frac{\lambda}{2} \) and minima when \( 2nd\cos r = m\lambda \).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Derivation of thin-film path difference and extrema
cards.tex: \Delta_{\text{geom}} = n(AB + BC) - AD, \quad AB = BC = \frac{d}{\cos r} \\ AC = 2d\tan r, \quad AD = AC\sin i = 2d\tan r \cdot (n\sin r) = \frac{2nd\sin^2 r}{\cos r} \\ \Delta_{\text{geom}} = \frac{2nd}{\cos r} - \frac{2nd\sin^2 r}{\cos r} = \frac{2nd(1 - \sin^2 r)}{\cos r} = 2nd\cos r \\ \text{Reflected total path difference: } \Delta = 2nd\cos r + \frac{\lambda}{2} \\ \text{Maxima (bright): } 2nd\cos r = (2m - 1)\frac{\lambda}{2}; \quad \text{Minima (dark): } 2nd\cos r = m\lambda
cards.body: Derive the geometric path difference 2nd \(\cos r\) using Snell's law \(\sin i = n \sin r\), add the \(\lambda/2\) reflection shift, and equate to \(m \lambda\) and \((2m+1)\lambda/2\). Diagram & geometry 6 · phase shift & conditions 5.

cards.label: Derivation
cards.title: Interference in a plane parallel film, step by step
cards.legend: A ray incident at \(A\) splits into the reflected ray \(AR_1\) and the internal ray \(ABC\), which emerges at \(C\) as \(CR_2\). The film has index \(\mu\) and thickness \(d\).

phases.name: Optical path difference
phases.why: compare the two reflected paths

phases.name: Trigonometric substitution
phases.why: express the lengths by d and the angles

phases.name: Snell's law simplification
phases.why: replace sin i by mu sin r

phases.name: Phase shift and extrema
phases.why: add lambda over 2 for the reflection

steps.note: Drop \(CD\) so that the two reflected paths beyond \(D\) are equal.

move.by: AB = BC = \frac{d}{\cos r},\ AD = 2d\tan r\sin i

steps.note: Each internal segment is \(d/\cos r\); the air path \(AD\) is \(2d\tan r\sin i\).

ask.q: What is the length of each internal segment \(AB\) and \(BC\)?
ask.why: The internal ray travels the film thickness \(d\) along a direction at angle \(r\) to the normal.

steps.note: Snell's law gives \(\sin i = \mu\sin r\), so the two terms combine.

ask.q: Which law is used to replace \(\sin i\) in \(AD = 2d\tan r\sin i\)?
ask.why: Snell's law links \(\sin i\) and \(\sin r\) through the film index \(\mu\).

steps.note: Use \(1 - \sin^2 r = \cos^2 r\); one \(\cos r\) cancels.

ask.q: Why is an extra path difference of \(\lambda/2\) added in reflected light?
ask.why: The ray reflected at the denser upper surface gains a phase shift of \(\pi\).

steps.note: Bright fringes satisfy this with integer \(m\); the thickness \(d\) sets the fringe order.

ask.q: What happens as the film thickness \(d \to 0\) in reflected light?
ask.why: At \(d=0\) the total path difference is \(\lambda/2\), which is a destructive condition.

cards.q: The geometric path difference between two rays reflected from a parallel film of thickness \( d \) and index \( n \) is ____.
cards.why: n(AB + BC) - AD simplifies to 2nd \(\cos r\).

cards.q: A phase change of \( \pi \) occurs when light is reflected at the boundary of an ____.
cards.why: Reflection from a medium of higher refractive index reverses the electric field phase by \(\pi\).

cards.q: The interference patterns in reflected and transmitted light from a non-absorbing thin film are ____.
cards.why: By conservation of energy, maxima in reflection correspond to minima in transmission.

sheets.title: Q1 · Focal length from system matrix (1 mark)

cards.label: PYQ · 1 mark
cards.title: Question 1
cards.q: The system matrix of a lens system is given by \(\begin{pmatrix} 9/5 & 1/100 \\ 8 & 3/5 \end{pmatrix}\). The focal length of the combination is _________ units.
Focal length f from matrix element -a (or -c)

options.t: 100 units (from \(P = -M12 = -1/100 => f = -100\), or magnitude 100 units; or \(1/8\) if \([y, \alpha]\) convention)

cards.why: In Ghatak's \([\lambda, y]\) convention M = \(\begin{pmatrix} b & -a \\ -d & c \end{pmatrix}\) where \(a = 1/f = -1/100\), giving \(|f| = 100\) units.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: 100 units (f = -100 units)
cards.body: Know first: The thin lens, principal foci and focal length. In the standard system matrix \( S = \begin{bmatrix} b & -a \\ -d & c \end{bmatrix} \) (with \( \det S = bc - ad = \frac{27}{25} - \frac{2}{25} = 1 \)), the optical power is \( P = a = -S_{12} = -\frac{1}{100} \), so the focal length has magnitude \( f = 100\text{ units} \) (\( -100\text{ units} \); or \( 1/8\text{ units} \) in the transposed convention).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Identification of focal length from matrix element
cards.tex: S = \begin{bmatrix} b & -a \\ -d & c \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 9/5 & 1/100 \\ 8 & 3/5 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \det S = \frac{27}{25} - \frac{8}{100} = 1 \\ -a = -\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{100} \implies f = -100\text{ units} \; (|f| = 100\text{ units})
cards.body: Read the power element \(a = 1/f\) from the off-diagonal entry -\(a = 1/100\). Answer 1.

cards.q: The determinant of the system matrix when the initial and final media are identical is ____.
cards.why: Every translation and refraction matrix has unit determinant (bc - ad = 1).

cards.q: In the system matrix \( \begin{bmatrix} b & -a \\ -d & c \end{bmatrix} \) for a thin lens, the element \( a \) equals ____.
cards.why: For a thin lens of focal length f, \(a = 1/f\) is the power.

cards.q: The reciprocal of the focal length of a lens system is called its ____.
cards.why: Power \(P = 1/f\) is measured in dioptres when f is in meters.

sheets.title: Q2 · Inner part of optical fiber (1 mark)

cards.label: PYQ · 1 mark
cards.title: Question 2
cards.q: The inner part of optical fiber is called _________.
Name of inner cylinder
cards.why: The central light-guiding cylinder of an optical fiber is called the core.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Core
cards.body: Know first: Laws of reflection and refraction from Fermat's principle. The inner cylindrical light-guiding region of an optical fiber, which has a higher refractive index \( n_1 \), is called the core.

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Optical fiber structure
cards.tex: r < a: \text{ Core } (n_1), \quad r > a: \text{ Cladding } (n_2 < n_1)
cards.body: State 'core'. Answer 1.

cards.q: The inner light-guiding region of an optical fiber is called the ____.
cards.why: Light is confined mainly within the high-index inner core.

cards.q: The refractive index of the core of an optical fiber is always ____.
options: slightly greater than that of the cladding
less than that of the cladding
cards.why: \(n1 > n2\) is required for total internal reflection at the core-cladding boundary.

cards.q: In a single-mode step-index fiber, the diameter of the core is typically around ____.
cards.why: Single-mode operation requires a very small core diameter comparable to a few wavelengths.

sheets.title: Q3 · Principle used in construction of hologram (1 mark)

cards.label: PYQ · 1 mark
cards.title: Question 3
cards.q: The construction of hologram made use of the principle of _________.
Physical principle of hologram construction
cards.why: Recording (constructing) a hologram uses interference between reference and object waves.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Interference of light
cards.body: Know first: Interference of light waves. The construction (recording) of a hologram makes use of the principle of interference between a coherent reference wave and the wave scattered by the object.

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Interference in hologram recording
cards.body: State interference of light. Answer 1.

cards.q: The recording (construction) of a hologram is based on the principle of ____.
cards.why: Coherent reference and object beams interfere on the recording plate.

cards.q: Reconstruction of the image from a hologram is based on the principle of ____.
cards.why: The developed fringe pattern diffracts the readout reference wave.

cards.q: To produce a stationary interference pattern during hologram construction, the two beams must be ____.
cards.why: Only coherent waves maintain a constant phase difference during exposure.

sheets.title: Q4 · Waves maintaining constant phase difference (1 mark)

cards.label: PYQ · 1 mark
cards.title: Question 4
cards.q: Two or more waves of the same frequency can maintain the same phase or constant phase difference over a distance and time are called _________.
Term for constant-phase waves
cards.why: Waves that maintain a constant phase relationship over space and time are called coherent waves.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Coherent waves
cards.body: Know first: Interference of light waves. Two or more waves of the same frequency that maintain the same phase or a constant phase difference over distance and time are called coherent waves.

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Coherence condition
cards.body: State 'coherent waves'. Answer 1.

cards.q: Two waves that maintain a constant phase difference over time are called ____.
cards.why: Coherence means a stable, predictable phase relationship.

cards.q: Two independent ordinary light bulbs cannot produce sustained interference fringes because they are ____.
cards.why: Independent thermal sources undergo random phase changes every ~\(10^{-8}\) s.

cards.q: In Young's double-slit experiment, coherent waves are obtained from a single source by division of ____.
cards.why: Two slits sample two portions of the same primary wavefront.

sheets.title: Q5 · Principal focal length equation of a zone plate (1 mark)

cards.label: PYQ · 1 mark
cards.title: Question 5
cards.q: The principal focal length of a zone plate is given by the equation _________.
Zone plate focal length formula
cards.why: The principal focal length is \(f = r_n^2 / (n \lambda) = r_1^2 / \lambda\).

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: \(f = r_n^2 / (n \lambda) = r_1^2 / \lambda\)
cards.body: Know first: Fresnel diffraction and zone plate (15). The principal focal length of a Fresnel zone plate is given by \( f = \frac{r_n^2}{n\lambda} = \frac{r_1^2}{\lambda} \), where \( r_n \) is the radius of the \( n \)-th zone and \( \lambda \) is the wavelength.

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Principal focal length expression
cards.body: Write \(f = r_n^2 / (n \lambda)\) or \(r_1^2 / \lambda\). Answer 1.

cards.q: The principal focal length of a zone plate is inversely proportional to the ____.
options: square of the first zone radius
cards.why: \(f = r1^2 / \lambda\) varies as \(1/\lambda\).

cards.q: For red light compared to violet light, the principal focal length of a zone plate is ____.
options: shorter for red than for violet
longer for red than for violet
cards.why: Since \(\lambda_{red} > \lambda_{violet}\) and \(f = r1^2 / \lambda\), \(f_{red} < f_{violet}\) (opposite to a glass lens).

cards.q: In the zone plate formula \( f = r_n^2 / (n\lambda) \), \( n \) denotes the ____.
cards.why: \(r_n\) is the outer radius of the n-th Fresnel half-period zone.

sheets.title: Q7 · Ray incident at angle greater than acceptance angle (1 mark)
sheets.source: PYQ Nov 2021 (D 10245) Q7 · also Nov 2022 (D 30197) Q6

cards.label: PYQ · 1 mark
cards.title: Question 7
cards.q: True or False : The light ray incident at an angle of incidence greater than acceptance angle on a step index fiber will be refracted through cladding.
True/False identification
cards.why: When incidence exceeds \(\theta_a\), the internal angle at the core-cladding wall is less than \(\theta_c\), so the ray refracts into the cladding.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: True
cards.body: Know first: Laws of reflection and refraction from Fermat's principle. The statement is True. A light ray entering the fiber core at an angle greater than the acceptance angle \( \theta_a \) strikes the core-cladding boundary at an angle of incidence smaller than the critical angle \( \theta_c \), and is therefore refracted out into the cladding.

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Condition for refraction into cladding
cards.body: State True because rays outside the acceptance cone do not undergo total internal reflection. Answer 1.

cards.q: When a ray enters a fiber at an angle smaller than the acceptance angle, at the core-cladding interface it undergoes ____.
cards.why: Rays inside the acceptance cone hit the wall at angles greater than \(\theta_c\).

cards.q: When a ray enters a fiber at an angle greater than the acceptance angle, its angle of incidence at the core-cladding wall is ____.
cards.why: Steeper entry gives a smaller angle of incidence with the normal to the cylindrical wall.

cards.q: Rays that refract into the cladding of an optical fiber are quickly ____.
cards.why: Cladding modes are stripped or lost at the outer coating.

sheets.title: Q9 · Cause of colours on a thin film and soap bubble (1 mark)
sheets.source: PYQ Nov 2021 (D 10245) Q9 · also Nov 2022 (D 30197) Q8, Nov 2018 Q6

cards.label: PYQ · 1 mark
cards.title: Question 9
cards.q: True or False : Colour appear on a thin film and on a soap bubble due to dispersion.
True/False identification
cards.why: Colours of thin films and soap bubbles are due to interference of light, not dispersion.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: False (due to interference)
cards.body: Know first: Colours of thin films, Newton's rings, Michelson interferometer (11). The statement is False. Brilliant colours appear on a thin oil film and on a soap bubble illuminated by white light due to interference by division of amplitude between waves reflected from the top and bottom surfaces of the film.

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Wavelength-selective thin-film interference
cards.body: State False because thin-film colours arise from interference, not dispersion. Answer 1.

cards.q: Colours seen on a thin soap bubble in white light are produced by ____.
cards.why: Reflections from the front and back surfaces of the thin film interfere.

cards.q: Splitting of white light into component colours by a glass prism is due to ____.
cards.why: In a prism, refractive index \(n(\lambda)\) varies with wavelength (dispersion).

cards.q: To observe vivid interference colours on a thin film, the source must be an ____.
cards.why: White light contains multiple wavelengths and an extended source allows viewing across the film.

sheets.title: Q10 · Velocity of O-ray and E-ray in a negative uniaxial crystal (1 mark)

cards.label: PYQ · 1 mark
cards.title: Question 10
cards.q: True or False : In a negative uniaxial crystal, velocity of O-ray is less than velocity of E-ray.
True/False identification
cards.why: In a negative uniaxial crystal (ne < no), \(v_o = c\)/no is less than \(v_e = c\)/ne (except along the optic axis).

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: True
cards.body: Know first: Double refraction and Huygens' explanation (20). The statement is True. In a negative uniaxial crystal (like calcite), \( n_e < n_o \), so the velocity of the ordinary ray \( v_o = c/n_o \) is less than the velocity of the extraordinary ray \( v_e \) in all directions except along the optic axis.

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Velocity inequality in negative crystal
cards.body: State True because \(n_o > n_e\) implies \(v_o < v_e\). Answer 1.

cards.q: In a negative uniaxial crystal, the ordinary refractive index \( n_o \) is ____.
cards.why: Negative birefringence means \(n_e - n_o < 0\), so \(n_o > n_e\).

cards.q: In a positive uniaxial crystal, the velocity of the O-ray compared to the E-ray (off the optic axis) is ____.
cards.why: In a positive crystal \(n_e > n_o\), so \(v_o = c/n_o > c/n_e = v_e\).

cards.q: The direction in a uniaxial crystal along which \( v_o = v_e \) is called the ____.
cards.why: No double refraction occurs for propagation along the optic axis.

sheets.title: Q12 · Advantages of matrix method in paraxial optics (2 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 2 marks
cards.title: Question 12
cards.q: What are the advantages of using matrix method in paraxial optics?
Systematic multiplication for multi-element systems and computer suitability

options.t: Reduces complex multi-lens ray tracing to 2x2 matrix multiplication, separates geometry from ray coordinates, and is ideal for computers

cards.why: State how 2x2 matrices simplify multi-surface optical systems and cardinal point calculations.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Advantages of matrix methods in paraxial optics
cards.body: Know first: The thin lens, principal foci and focal length. Using \( 2\times 2 \) ray-transfer matrices reduces ray tracing through a complex multi-element optical system to simple sequential multiplication of translation and refraction matrices (\( S = M_n \dots M_2 M_1 \)). The system matrix depends only on the optical system parameters (not the input ray), directly gives the focal lengths and cardinal points, and is ideally suited for fast computer computation.

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Sequential matrix multiplication
cards.tex: \begin{bmatrix} \lambda_2 \\ y_2 \end{bmatrix} = S \begin{bmatrix} \lambda_1 \\ y_1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad S = M_N \dots M_2 M_1, \quad \det S = 1
cards.body: State that any cascade of lenses and spaces is represented by one 2x2 product matrix and det\((S) = 1\) provides a built-in algebraic check. Advantages 2.

cards.q: In paraxial matrix optics, each translation or refraction operation is represented by a ____.
cards.why: Two paraxial coordinates (y and \(n\cdot\theta\)) require a 2x2 transformation matrix.

cards.q: If a ray passes through elements \( M_1, M_2, M_3 \) in that order, the overall system matrix is ____.
cards.why: Matrices are multiplied in reverse order from right to left as the ray progresses.

cards.q: The condition \( \det(S) = bc - ad = 1 \) serves as a convenient check on ____.
options: algebraic accuracy of the system matrix
cards.why: Because each elementary matrix has determinant 1, their product must also have determinant 1.

sheets.title: Q13 · Conditions for sustained interference pattern (2 marks)
sheets.source: PYQ Nov 2021 (D 10245) Q13 · also Nov 2022 (CBCSS) Q3, Nov 2022 (D 30197) Q13, Nov 2018 Q20

cards.label: PYQ · 2 marks
cards.title: Question 13
cards.q: Describe the conditions to obtain sustained interference pattern.
Coherence, same frequency/wavelength, equal amplitudes, small d and large D

options.t: At least four conditions (coherent sources, same frequency/wavelength, nearly equal amplitudes, small d, large D) stated

cards.why: List the essential conditions for a stationary, high-contrast, well-spaced interference pattern.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Conditions for sustained interference
cards.body: Know first: Interference of light waves. To obtain a sustained, distinct interference pattern: (1) the two sources must be coherent (maintain a constant phase difference) and emit continuous waves of the same frequency/wavelength; (2) their amplitudes should be equal or nearly equal for high contrast (\( I_{\min} \approx 0 \)); (3) the separation \( d \) between the sources must be small and the screen distance \( D \) large; and (4) if polarized, the waves must be in the same state of polarization.

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Summary of interference conditions
cards.tex: 1.\; \phi_1 - \phi_2 = \text{constant (coherent)}, \quad \lambda_1 = \lambda_2 \\ 2.\; a_1 = a_2 \implies I_{\min} = (a_1 - a_2)^2 = 0 \\ 3.\; \beta = \frac{\lambda D}{d} \text{ large} \implies d \text{ small, } D \text{ large}
cards.body: State the coherence/monochromaticity condition, equal-amplitude contrast condition, and geometric spacing condition. Conditions 2.

cards.q: For the dark fringes in an interference pattern to be completely dark, the two interfering waves must have ____.
For an interference pattern to remain stationary in time (sustained), the two sources must be ____.
cards.why: Constant phase difference keeps the positions of maxima and minima fixed in time.

cards.q: Two orthogonally polarized light beams cannot form interference fringes because their electric vectors are ____.
cards.why: The dot product E1 . E2 of perpendicular vectors is zero.

sheets.title: Q15 · Overlapping spectra in a diffraction grating (2 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 2 marks
cards.title: Question 15
cards.q: What is meant by overlapping spectra in the spectra of a grating?
Condition \(m1 \lambda1 = m2 \lambda2\) and visible spectrum overlap example

options.t: Coincidence of different wavelengths in different orders \((m1 \lambda1 = m2 \lambda2)\) explained with visible range example

cards.why: Explain how \(m1 \lambda1 = m2 \lambda2\) causes higher-order spectra of short wavelengths to overlap lower-order spectra of long wavelengths.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Overlapping of grating spectra
cards.body: Know first: N-slit Fraunhofer diffraction pattern and grating (14). In a diffraction grating, where \( d\sin\theta = m\lambda \), a wavelength \( \lambda_1 \) in order \( m_1 \) appears at the same diffraction angle \( \theta \) as another wavelength \( \lambda_2 \) in order \( m_2 \) whenever \( m_1\lambda_1 = m_2\lambda_2 \). For white light (\( 4000\text{ \AA} \) to \( 7000\text{ \AA} \)), the first-order spectrum is separate, but the red end of the second order (\( 2\times 7000 = 14000\text{ \AA} \)) overlaps the violet/blue end of the third order (\( 3\times 4000 = 12000\text{ \AA} \)).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Condition for spectral overlap
cards.body: Write the overlap condition \(m1 \lambda1 = m2 \lambda2\) and show that second-order red overlaps third-order violet. Condition 1 · example 1.

cards.q: In a grating illuminated with white light, two wavelengths \( \lambda_1 \) and \( \lambda_2 \) in orders \( m_1 \) and \( m_2 \) overlap when ____.
cards.why: Both satisfy \(d \sin(\theta) = m1 \lambda1 = m2 \lambda2\) at the same angle \(\theta\).

cards.q: For visible white light (400 nm to 700 nm), overlapping of grating spectra begins between the ____.
cards.why: First order ends at 700 nm and second begins at \(2\cdot400 = 800\) nm (no overlap), but \(2\cdot700 = 1400\) nm > \(3\cdot400 = 1200\) nm.

cards.q: The second-order line of wavelength \( 6000\text{ \AA} \) coincides in angle with the third-order line of wavelength ____.

sheets.title: Q18 · System matrix for thin lens and thin lens formula (4 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 4 marks
cards.title: Question 18
cards.q: Obtain system matrix for thin film and hence obtain thin lens formula.
Product of two spherical refraction matrices to get thin-lens system matrix

options.t: Refraction matrices R1 and R2 multiplied for \(t -> 0\) to obtain S = \(\begin{pmatrix} 1 & -P \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\) with \(P = (n-1)(1/R1 - 1/R2)\)
Final matrix stated without multiplying \(R2 \cdot R1\)

cards.why: Multiply the two refraction matrices at R1 and R2 with thickness \(t = 0\).

cards.q: Derivation of thin lens formula \(1/v - 1/u = 1/f\) from the system matrix

options.t: Translation to object/image planes applied and \(1/v - 1/u = (n-1)(1/R1 - 1/R2) = 1/f\) obtained
Formula stated without connecting to matrix

cards.why: Apply the imaging condition between object plane u and image plane v to deduce \(1/v - 1/u = 1/f\).

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Thin-lens system matrix and lens formula
cards.body: Know first: The thin lens, principal foci and focal length. Multiplying the refraction matrices of the two spherical surfaces of radii \( R_1 \) and \( R_2 \) (with thickness \( t \to 0 \) and \( n_1 = 1, n_2 = n \)) gives the thin-lens system matrix \( S = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1/f \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \), where \( \frac{1}{f} = (n - 1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right) \). Including object translation \( -u \) and image translation \( v \), the imaging condition yields the thin lens formula \( \frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f} \).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Matrix derivation of thin lens formula
cards.tex: \mathcal{R}_1 = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -P_1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathcal{R}_2 = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -P_2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad P_1 = \frac{n - 1}{R_1}, \quad P_2 = \frac{1 - n}{R_2} \\ S = \mathcal{R}_2 \mathcal{R}_1 = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -(P_1 + P_2) \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1/f \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \frac{1}{f} = (n - 1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right) \\ \text{Object-to-image matrix: } \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ v & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1/f \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ -u & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 + u/f & -1/f \\ v - u + uv/f & 1 - v/f \end{bmatrix} \\ \text{Image condition } (M_{21} = 0): \quad v - u + \frac{uv}{f} = 0 \implies \frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}
cards.body: Multiply the two surface refraction matrices to find S, then sandwich S between object and image translation matrices and set the (2,1) element to zero. System matrix 2 · thin lens formula 2.

cards.label: Derivation
cards.title: System matrix and thin lens formula, step by step
cards.legend: Thin lens of index \(n\) and radii \(R_1, R_2\) in air, imaging object at distance \(u\) to image at distance \(v\). \(P\) is the lens power.

phases.name: Surface refraction matrices
phases.why: one matrix per spherical surface

phases.name: Thin-lens product
phases.why: let the thickness go to zero

phases.name: Object-image translation
phases.why: add the free-space translations

phases.name: Imaging condition
phases.why: the element M12 must vanish

steps.note: Refraction matrix of the first surface, from air into the lens of index \(n\).
Second surface, from the lens (index \(n\)) back into air.

ask.q: Why is the internal translation between the two surfaces the identity matrix?
ask.why: For a thin lens the translation \(t \to 0\) gives \([1, 0; 0, 1]\).

steps.note: The product gives \(P = \frac{1}{f} = (n-1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right)\).

ask.q: Which element of the thin-lens system matrix \(\mathcal{S}\) equals \(-P\)?
ask.why: In the product, the lower-left element carries the power \(-P\).

steps.note: Free-space translations \(\mathcal{T}\) carry the ray from object to lens and lens to image.

ask.q: Which translation matrix is used for a distance \(u\) in air?
ask.why: A translation by \(u\) in air keeps the slope and adds \(u\) times the slope to the height.

steps.tex: M_{12} = u + v - P u v
steps.note: Multiply out the three matrices; only the (1,2) element matters for imaging.

ask.q: Which element of the overall matrix must vanish for point-to-point imaging?
ask.why: Zero \(M_{12}\) means all rays from one point meet at one image point.

steps.note: Set \(M_{12} = 0\) for the imaging condition.
Divide each term by \(uv\).
The thin lens formula, with \(P = 1/f\).

cards.q: The refraction matrix of a single spherical surface of power \( P = (n_2 - n_1)/R \) is ____.
cards.why: At a refracting boundary \(y2 = y1\) and \(\lambda2 = \lambda1 - P y1\).

cards.q: Across a thin lens of zero thickness, the ray height \( y \) ____.
cards.why: With \(t -> 0\), a thin lens bends the ray slope without changing its height at the lens plane.

cards.q: The total optical power \( P \) of a thin lens is the sum of the ____.
options: powers of its two refracting surfaces

sheets.title: Q19 · Fresnel's biprism and determination of wavelength (4 marks)
sheets.source: PYQ Nov 2021 (D 10245) Q19 · also Nov 2020 Q19

cards.label: PYQ · 4 marks
cards.title: Question 19
cards.q: Describe Fresnel's biprism. Explain how the wavelength of light can be determined with the help of it.
Construction of biprism and formation of virtual coherent sources

options.t: Obtuse prism (~179 deg) with base angles ~30', ray diagram, and formation of S1, S2 explained

cards.why: Describe the biprism geometry and draw how it forms two virtual sources S1 and S2.

cards.q: Measurement of \(\beta\), D, and d (displacement method or formula) to find \(\lambda\)

options.t: Formula \(\lambda = \beta d / D\) and measurement of \(\beta\), \(D = a+b\), and \(d = 2a(n-1)\alpha\) or \(\sqrt{d1 d2}\) explained

cards.why: Explain how \(\beta\), D, and d are measured on an optical bench to compute \(\lambda = \beta d / D\).

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Fresnel's biprism and wavelength measurement
cards.body: Know first: Fresnel's two-mirror and Fresnel's biprism. Fresnel's biprism consists of two acute-angled thin prisms joined base-to-base (obtuse angle \( \approx 179^\circ \), acute base angles \( \alpha \approx 30' \)). Light from a narrow vertical slit \( S \) at distance \( a \) is refracted by the two halves to form two virtual coherent sources \( S_1, S_2 \) separated by \( d = 2a(n - 1)\alpha \). Measuring the fringe width \( \beta \) with a micrometer eyepiece at distance \( D = a + b \) and finding \( d = \sqrt{d_1 d_2} \) by the convex-lens displacement method gives \( \lambda = \frac{\beta d}{D} \).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Wavelength determination formulas
cards.tex: d = 2a(n - 1)\alpha \quad \text{or} \quad d = \sqrt{d_1 d_2} \text{ (conjugate lens positions)} \\ D = a + b \\ \beta = \frac{\lambda D}{d} \implies \lambda = \frac{\beta d}{D}
cards.body: Draw the biprism ray diagram, write the virtual slit separation d, and explain the measurement of \(\beta\), D, and d. Description & diagram 2 · wavelength determination 2.

cards.q: The obtuse angle of a standard Fresnel biprism is approximately ____.
cards.why: Very small base angles (~30') keep the virtual sources close together so fringes are wide.

cards.q: In the displacement method with a convex lens in a biprism experiment, the source separation \( d \) equals ____.
cards.why: Since \(m1 \cdot m2 = (d1/d)(d2/d) = 1\) for conjugate positions, \(d = \sqrt{d1 d2}\).

cards.q: In Fresnel's biprism experiment, the central zero-order fringe with white light is ____.
cards.why: Both refracted paths traverse equal thicknesses of glass, so all wavelengths arrive in phase at the center.

sheets.title: Q20 · Michelson interferometer and wavelength difference of two waves (4 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 4 marks
cards.title: Question 20
cards.q: With neat diagram, explain Michelson's interferometer. Describe how it can be used to determine the difference in wavelength of two waves.
Neat diagram and explanation of Michelson interferometer

options.t: Diagram with M1, M2, G1, G2 and explanation of amplitude division

cards.why: Draw the interferometer and explain the roles of G1, G2, M1, and M2.

cards.q: Determination of wavelength difference \(\Delta \lambda = \lambda^2 / (2 \Delta d)\)

options.t: Discordance/consonance method and derivation of \(\Delta \lambda = \lambda1 \lambda2 / (2 \Delta d) \approx \lambda^2 / (2 \Delta d)\)

cards.why: Use \(2 \Delta d = m \lambda1 = (m+1) \lambda2\) between successive maximum-contrast positions.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Michelson interferometer and doublet wavelength difference
cards.body: Know first: Colours of thin films, Newton's rings, Michelson interferometer (11). In a Michelson interferometer, beam splitter \( G_1 \) divides the incident beam between mirrors \( M_1 \) and \( M_2 \). When the source emits two close wavelengths \( \lambda_1 \) and \( \lambda_2 \) (such as the sodium D lines), moving \( M_1 \) through a distance \( \Delta d \) between two successive positions of maximum distinctness (or minimum contrast) shifts one pattern by \( m \) fringes and the other by \( m + 1 \) fringes: \( 2\Delta d = m\lambda_1 = (m+1)\lambda_2 \), giving \( \Delta\lambda = \lambda_1 - \lambda_2 \approx \frac{\lambda^2}{2\Delta d} \).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Derivation of wavelength difference formula
cards.tex: 2\Delta d = m\lambda_1 = (m + 1)\lambda_2 \implies m = \frac{2\Delta d}{\lambda_1}, \quad m + 1 = \frac{2\Delta d}{\lambda_2} \\ (m + 1) - m = 1 = 2\Delta d\left(\frac{1}{\lambda_2} - \frac{1}{\lambda_1}\right) = \frac{2\Delta d(\lambda_1 - \lambda_2)}{\lambda_1 \lambda_2} \\ \Delta\lambda = \lambda_1 - \lambda_2 = \frac{\lambda_{\text{avg}}^2}{2\Delta d}
cards.body: Explain the interferometer setup with diagram, then equate the mirror displacement \(2 \Delta d\) between successive beat maxima to derive \(\Delta \lambda\). Diagram & setup 2 · \(\Delta \lambda\) derivation 2.

cards.q: In a Michelson interferometer, the difference between two close wavelengths \( \Delta\lambda \) is given by ____.
cards.why: From \(2 \Delta d (\Delta \lambda / \lambda^2) = 1\), we get \(\Delta \lambda = \lambda^2 / (2 \Delta d)\).

cards.q: Between two successive positions of maximum fringe visibility for a doublet, the number of fringes of \( \lambda_2 \) exceeds that of \( \lambda_1 \) by ____.
cards.why: The faster-oscillating pattern gains exactly one full fringe over the other.

cards.q: When the maxima of \( \lambda_1 \) fall on the minima of \( \lambda_2 \), the fringe contrast is ____.
cards.why: Out-of-step superposition of the two fringe systems produces uniform illumination.

sheets.title: Q22 · Intensity distribution of Fresnel diffraction at a straight edge (4 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 4 marks
cards.title: Question 22
cards.q: Draw the intensity distribution curve of Fresnel's diffraction at a straight edge and explain it.
Intensity distribution curve and explanation of shadow and illuminated regions

options.t: Neat intensity curve drawn, showing \(1/4\) intensity at geometric shadow edge, damped oscillations in illuminated region, and monotonic decay into shadow

cards.why: Draw the intensity profile across the geometric shadow boundary and explain both regions.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Fresnel diffraction at a straight edge
cards.body: Know first: Fresnel diffraction by a straight edge (16). When cylindrical waves pass a sharp straight edge, the intensity at the exact boundary of the geometrical shadow is one-fourth of the unobstructed intensity (\( I = I_0/4 \), since half the wavefront is blocked). Inside the geometrical shadow, the intensity falls off monotonically and rapidly to zero without any maxima or minima. In the illuminated region above the edge, alternate exposure of odd and even numbers of half-period strips produces parallel bright and dark fringes of decreasing contrast that approach uniform intensity \( I_0 \).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Half-period strip analysis for straight edge
cards.tex: A_{\text{edge}} = \frac{A_0}{2} \implies I_{\text{edge}} = \frac{I_0}{4} \\ \text{Illuminated region: } \begin{cases} \text{Odd strips exposed } \to \text{maxima } (I > I_0) \\ \text{Even strips exposed } \to \text{minima } (I < I_0) \end{cases} \\ \text{Shadow region: } I \to 0 \text{ monotonically}
cards.body: Sketch I(x) vs position x showing \(I0/4\) at \(x = 0\), monotonic decay for \(x < 0\), and damped oscillations around I0 for \(x > 0\). Intensity curve 2 · explanation of regions 2.

cards.q: At the exact boundary of the geometrical shadow of a straight edge, the light intensity is ____.
options: one-fourth of the unobstructed intensity I0
cards.why: Half the wavefront is blocked, reducing the amplitude to \(A0/2\) and intensity to \(I0/4\).

cards.q: Inside the geometrical shadow of a straight edge, the light intensity ____.
options: decreases monotonically to zero without fringes
oscillates with bright and dark fringes
cards.why: Progressively higher-order half-period strips cancel smoothly without sign reversals.

cards.q: In the illuminated region near a straight edge, the spacing between successive diffraction fringes ____.
options: decreases as we move away from the shadow edge
increases as we move away from the shadow edge
cards.why: Fringe positions vary as \(\sqrt{n}\), so fringes crowd closer together farther from the edge.

sheets.title: Q23 · Quarter-wave plate and half-wave plate (4 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 4 marks
cards.title: Question 23
cards.q: Write brief note on (a) Quarter wave plate ; (b) Half wave plate.
Definition, thickness formula, and uses of Quarter-Wave Plate (QWP)

options.t: Path difference \(\lambda/4\) (phase \(\pi/2\)), thickness \(d = \lambda / [4|n_e - n_o|]\), and use for circular/elliptical polarization stated

cards.why: Define QWP, write its thickness formula, and state its function.

cards.q: Definition, thickness formula, and uses of Half-Wave Plate (HWP)

options.t: Path difference \(\lambda/2\) (phase \(\pi\)), thickness \(d = \lambda / [2|n_e - n_o|]\), and rotation of polarization plane by \(2 \theta\) stated

cards.why: Define HWP, write its thickness formula, and state its effect on polarization.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Quarter-wave plate (QWP) and half-wave plate (HWP)
cards.body: Know first: Quarter-wave and half-wave plates (21). (a) A Quarter-Wave Plate is a doubly refracting crystal plate cut with its optic axis parallel to the surface, of thickness \( d = \frac{\lambda_0}{4|n_o - n_e|} \), which introduces a path difference of \( \lambda_0/4 \) (phase difference \( \pi/2 \)) between the o-ray and e-ray; it converts linearly polarized light into circularly or elliptically polarized light and vice versa. (b) A Half-Wave Plate has thickness \( d = \frac{\lambda_0}{2|n_o - n_e|} \), introducing a path difference of \( \lambda_0/2 \) (phase difference \( \pi \)); it rotates the plane of linear polarization by \( 2\phi \) and reverses the handedness of circularly polarized light.

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Thickness and phase formulas for wave plates
cards.tex: \text{(a) QWP: } |n_o - n_e|d = (2m + 1)\frac{\lambda_0}{4}, \quad \Delta\phi = \frac{\pi}{2}, \quad d_{\min} = \frac{\lambda_0}{4|n_o - n_e|} \\ \text{(b) HWP: } |n_o - n_e|d = (2m + 1)\frac{\lambda_0}{2}, \quad \Delta\phi = \pi, \quad d_{\min} = \frac{\lambda_0}{2|n_o - n_e|}
cards.body: State the cut orientation, path/phase difference, minimum thickness formula, and optical applications of both plates. QWP 2 · HWP 2.

cards.q: In both quarter-wave and half-wave plates, the crystal is cut with its optic axis ____.
cards.why: When the optic axis is parallel to the surface, o- and e-rays travel along the same path at different speeds.

cards.q: When left-circularly polarized light passes normally through a half-wave plate, it emerges as ____.
cards.why: A phase shift of \(\pi\) reverses the relative phase of the orthogonal components, inverting handedness.

cards.q: When linearly polarized light oriented at \( 45^\circ \) to the optic axis passes through a quarter-wave plate, it becomes ____.
cards.why: Equal orthogonal amplitudes with \(a \pi/2\) phase difference produce circularly polarized light.

sheets.title: Q24 · Necessity of cladding and applications of optical fiber (4 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 4 marks
cards.title: Question 24
cards.q: Give the necessity of cladding in the optical fiber. Also mention any four applications of optical fiber.
Functions/necessity of the cladding layer

options.t: Provides clean TIR interface, prevents crosstalk between fibers, protects core from surface contamination/scattering, and reduces NA to limit dispersion

cards.why: State why a bare core is impractical and how cladding ensures low-loss guidance.

cards.q: Four applications of optical fibers

options.t: Four applications (telecommunications, medical endoscopy, fiber sensors, military/avionics/networking) listed

cards.why: List four distinct applications of optical fibers.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Necessity of cladding and applications of optical fibers
cards.body: Know first: Laws of reflection and refraction from Fermat's principle. Necessity of cladding: (1) provides a clean, protected dielectric interface of controlled refractive index \( n_2 < n_1 \) for total internal reflection; (2) prevents light leakage and crosstalk between adjacent fibers in a bundle; (3) protects the core from surface scratches, moisture, and dust; and (4) keeps \( n_1 - n_2 \) small to reduce modal dispersion. Four applications: (1) high-speed long-haul telecommunication and internet links, (2) medical endoscopy and laser surgery, (3) fiber optic sensors (gyroscopes, temperature/strain sensors), and (4) industrial inspection and local area networks.
cards.tex: n_2 < n_1 \text{ (controlled TIR)}, \quad \text{Telecom, Endoscopy, Sensors, Networking}

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Role of cladding index n2
cards.body: List four reasons why cladding is necessary and four practical applications of optical fibers. Cladding necessity 2 · four applications 2.

cards.q: In a bundle of optical fibers, the cladding prevents light from leaking from one fiber core into another, a problem known as ____.
cards.why: Cladding isolates the evanescent field of each core from neighbouring fibers.

cards.q: Flexible coherent bundles of optical fibers are used in medicine to view internal organs in an instrument called an ____.
cards.why: An endoscope transmits illumination and images through flexible fiber bundles.

cards.q: By making the cladding refractive index \( n_2 \) only slightly smaller than \( n_1 \), the intermodal dispersion is ____.
cards.why: Pulse broadening \(\Delta \tau\) is proportional to \((n1 - n2)\).

sheets.title: Q25 · System matrix and focal length of a glass lens (4 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 4 marks
cards.title: Question 25
cards.q: Obtain a system matrix for a lens placed in air made of glass of refractive index 1.6 and radii of curvature 60 cm each. Find the focal length of the lens?
Calculation of focal length f and system matrix S

options.t: Focal length \(f = 50\) cm found without writing the 2x2 matrix

cards.why: For a biconvex lens of radii 60 cm each, \(R1 = +60\) cm and \(R2 = -60\) cm, so \(f = 50\) cm.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Focal length \(f = 50\) cm and S = \(\begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1/50 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\)
cards.body: Know first: The thin lens, principal foci and focal length.
